Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Nimbus looks like a strong fit for the pilot we discussed. Procurement asked for a slightly different invoice cadence to match your fiscal calendar. - Contract value: $480,000 over 12 months (pilot + reserved capacity)
- Invoicing cadence: quarterly invoices (4x) aligned to calendar quarter ends
- Payment terms: Net-90 from invoice date
- One-time kickoff invoice: optional 5% carryover to first invoice or net due on signature (open to your preference)

I’ve attached the current SOW and a suggested payment schedule for reference. If procurement needs a formal PO or a billing contact, can you share their email?

Attachments: [Nimbus_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf)], [Proposed_Payment_Schedule.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Aditya / Michael —

I reviewed the procurement form and the SOW. Legal is OK with accommodating a quarterly invoice cadence and Net-90 in principle, provided we get the following baked into the agreement: 

1) PO acceptance: add a clause that the PO confirms purchase but payment terms are governed by Redwood’s invoice; PO is accepted for order processing but does not supersede Redwood’s payment terms unless explicitly agreed in writing.
2) Late payment: Standard interest at 1.5% per month after Net-60 (we avoid silent extension to Net-120).
3) Security/compliance: include SOC 2 attestation reference (we already have this on file) and include a data-processing addendum (DPA) if PHI processing is in scope.
4) Mitigation: require a customer PO or signed DocuSign prior to provisioning; if PO delayed >60 days past effective date, we reserve the right to pause service.

Regarding the requested 5% concession for Net-90: legal can include a conditional clause that the concession is tied to obtaining a PO within 30 days and an approved credit hold release once payment history is established.

If finance signs off on the credit exposure and discount, I’m comfortable with an amendment that includes the above. I can draft the clause language for the payment schedule.

—Monica

Subject: Re: Fwd: Deferred invoice plan & Net-90 request for Nimbus Health — finance assessment

Team —

Quick finance read: granting Net-90 on a $480k ARR deal increases our DSO risk materially but is manageable with conditions. Proposed finance guardrails: 
- Require customer PO prior to first invoice (procurement confirmed they will issue).
- Require a 5% invoice reserve (holdback) to be offset against the last invoice if all payments are timely. Equivalent to $24k on this deal.
- Alternatively, if the business insists on no upfront, require a partial prepayment of 5% on execution (we prefer partial prepay).
- Approve Net-90 for the first 2 quarters as a trial; after two clean quarters we can re-evaluate credit terms.

Regarding the commercial concession: the requested 5% discount tied to extended terms is high. Finance can approve a 3% one-time concession (not recurring) provided we add: (a) PO prior to provisioning, (b) payment holdback or 5% prepay, and (c) accelerated late fee at 1.5%/month starting at day 61.

If Sales prefers to keep 5% concession, we need an exec-level sign-off from VP Sales or CFO — otherwise approve 3%.

I can sign off on Net-90 + quarterly invoicing given the above guardrails. Monica, if you can add the contract language for the holdback and PO clause, we should be ready to move.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance
michael.grant@redwood.inference.com
